newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares extend losses, Wall Street weighs.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares extend losses, Wall Street weighs.

text.p: Italian stocks continued their downward technical correction on Thursday, closing just off session lows with sentiment depressed by Dow weakness in a market still shuddering from the aftershocks of U.S. Fed chairman Greenspan's latest warning Wednesday that Wall Street was reaching unsustainable levels.

Traders said telecoms stocks again came under pressure with Telecom Italia, the most traded stock with over 25 million shares changing hands, losing 3.12 percent to 4,065 lire on mainly foreign sell orders, traders said.
The All-share Mibtel index ended 1.27 pct down at 11,929 after a low at 11,879 while the Mib30 blue chip index closed 1.45 pct off at 17,727 after touching a 17,634 low.
Easier bond futures amid EMU worries and domestic political uncertainty were also weighing on sentiment.
"It's a market without any fresh ideas. We're seeing very selective business, mainly of sell orders," one trader said.
Energy group ENI shed 1.43 percent to 8,550 lire and Fiat lost 1.9 percent to 5,100, mainly in line with the bourse index, but Olivetti gained a modest 0.56 percent to 623 lire.
Telecoms holding Stet fell 3.06 percent to 7,510 and mobile phone operator TIM lost 1.52 percent to 4,595 lire.
In banks, Ambroveneto lost 2.29 percent to 4,100 and BCI slipped 0.48 percent to 3,500 lire.
